newsitem.title: DENMARK: FORECAST - Denmark sees lower 1997 budget deficit.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Denmark sees lower 1997 budget deficit.

text.p: Denmark's Finance Ministry provisionally cut on Monday its previous estimate for the 1997 state budget deficit by approximately seven billion crowns from 19.3 billion crowns in its last forecast in October.
The new estimate was released after the Social Democrat-led minority coalition government in recent days secured a parliamentary majority for its budget for next year with opposition support.
The new figure cuts Denmark's expected state budget deficit to around 12 billion crowns in 1997, against the 28.5 billion crown shortfall for 1996 the ministry forecast in October.

In a statement the ministry said the effect of the government's deals with opposition parties on the 1997 state budget would be that the expected shortfall would fall by some seven billion crowns, adding that a new official forecast would be published on December 17.

After weeks of complex negotiations, the centre-left government was assured a majority for its 1997 state budget on Sunday when the radical, anti-establishment Unity List, which has six seats in Denmark's 179-seat parliamemt, decided to abstain from voting for the finance bill.
A Unity List decision to vote against the budget would have triggered an onslaught on the government by right-wing parties led by the Liberals, which have long been waiting for a chance to topple it.
Last week, the government signed a tactical agreement with the far-left Socialist Peoples' Party winning guarantees of its support for the budget.
Denmark's 1997 state budget will now be formally passed by parliament on December 19, before the house adjourns for the Christmas recess.
